Scribing platform for senior design

A 3D printer repurposed as an automated substrate scribing platform.

My role
CAD Lead
Context
Senior design, Aug to Dec 2026
Software
SolidWorks, MATLAB

Our team is building an automated platform for subtractive thin-film patterning by repurposing a 3D printer to scribe thin films on glass substrates. As CAD Lead, I kept the full SolidWorks assembly organized as six subsystems came together.

  • An assembly of more than 1,000 part files, organized into six subsystems: XYZ motion frame, substrate mount, scribing toolhead, toolhead replacement, spatial detection, and a modular base.
  • MATLAB trade studies compared design options before the design was finalized.

SLA and FDM feature plates

A test part comparing how FDM and SLA printers handle the same features.

My role
Designer, with a partner
Context
Additive manufacturing class
Software
SolidWorks, BambuLab FDM, Formlabs SLA

With a partner, I modeled a plate with flat and slanted surfaces, concave and convex curves, fins, slots, pillars, holes, and an overhang. We printed it on a BambuLab FDM printer and on Formlabs Form 3 and Form 4 SLA printers, then measured accuracy and surface finish.

  • Average pillar dimension error: FDM 6.7%, Form 3 2.2%, Form 4 2.6%. The smallest pillar (0.025 in) was off by 24% on FDM.
  • Surface roughness, measured with a Filmetrics machine, was generally lower on SLA. The concave curve measured about 52.8 µm on FDM versus 7.2 µm on the Form 4.

Marble track

A single-piece, no-assembly marble maze designed for 3D printing.

My role
Designer, with a partner
Context
Additive manufacturing class
Software
SolidWorks, FDM 3D printing

To show what additive manufacturing does well, we designed a marble track that prints as one part with no assembly. The marble runs through a maze, around the back through a tube, and into a plinko board, where it can fall off, loop back to the maze, or exit at the end.

  • Requirements: under 4 in in every direction, under 5 in³ of material, one part, and little post-processing.
  • A weighted decision matrix chose FDM, which scored 287 against 257 for Form 3 and 259 for Form 4.
  • Every major feature printed within 5% of its nominal size. The worst case was the 0.05 in maze wall at 4.0%.
  • Estimated print cost was about $1.60, compared with roughly $3.00 to $3.40 for traditionally made marble mazes.

About me

I’m a mechanical engineering student at the University of Notre Dame, graduating in May 2027 with a minor in data science. I like projects where a design has to work in the real world: modeled carefully, built, tested, and improved.

My CAD experience runs from team projects and research to my senior design project, where I serve as CAD Lead on an assembly of more than 1,000 parts. I’m a certified CAD Design Associate.

Data science is what sets me apart from a typical mechanical engineer. I’ve run MATLAB trade studies to compare designs, interned as a data analyst at FB Holdings, and used SQL and Power BI to turn large datasets into clear answers. In the lab I’ve worked with Arduino, sensors, and heat transfer simulations in SolidWorks.

Away from the drafting table, I direct academic talks for my dorm, St. Edward’s Hall, and play intramural hockey. Our hall won the championship in 2024 and 2026.
